answer_key_points: Data consistency is maintained with a multiversion model (Multiversion Concurrency Control, MVCC): each SQL statement sees a snapshot of data as it was some time ago, regardless of the current state of the underlying data, which prevents statements from viewing inconsistent data and provides transaction isolation for each database session.

The main advantage of MVCC over locking is that locks acquired for querying (reading) data do not conflict with locks acquired for writing data, so reading never blocks writing and writing never blocks reading; PostgreSQL maintains this guarantee even at the Serializable Snapshot Isolation (SSI) level.

answer_key_points: Only B-tree indexes can produce sorted output; a forward scan of an index on column x produces output satisfying ORDER BY x (ascending, with nulls last by default), and the index can also be scanned backward for descending order. The planner chooses between satisfying an ORDER BY via an index scan or an explicit sort, and indexes are most useful when only a few rows are needed, especially for ORDER BY combined with LIMIT.

PostgreSQL supports index-only scans, which can answer queries from the index alone without any heap access, returning values directly out of each index entry. Two fundamental restrictions apply: the index type must support index-only scans (B-tree indexes always do; GiST and SP-GiST support them only for some operator classes), and the query must reference only columns stored in the index.

answer_key_points: A column can be assigned a default value: when a new row is created and no values are specified for some of the columns, those columns are filled with their respective default values, and if no default is declared explicitly the default value is the null value.

An identity column is a special column generated automatically from an implicit sequence and used to generate key values; if an INSERT on the table specifies no value for the identity column, a value generated by the implicit sequence is inserted, and the keyword DEFAULT can be specified in INSERT or UPDATE to explicitly request the sequence-generated value.
